title: Local model of a weak-equivalence representable presheaf
statement:
Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category with functorial factorizations in the sense of [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping], and let $q:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M_\infty$ be its homotopy coherent localization. Use the locally constant presheaf model category $P_{\mathrm{lc}}(C)$ of [lem-coef-locally-constant-presheaf-slice]. Let $\mathcal U$ be a full subcategory of $\mathcal M$ whose object class is closed under weak equivalences in both directions. Let $C=w\mathcal U$ have those objects and just the weak-equivalence arrows; enlarge universes so $C$ is small. For $x\in\mathcal U$ put $h_x(y)=W_{\mathcal M}(y,x)$, the discrete simplicial presheaf of actual weak equivalences. There exists a fibrant object $E_x\in P_{\mathrm{lc}}(C)$ and a local weak equivalence $h_x\to E_x$ with natural weak homotopy equivalences
$$E_x(y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}^{\mathrm{eq}}_{\mathcal M_\infty}(qy,qx),$$
where the superscript means the union of the components consisting of equivalences in the derived mapping space. A local weak equivalence means a map inducing weak equivalences of derived mapping spaces into every objectwise Kan presheaf that inverts every arrow of $C$. The comparison on actual weak equivalences is induced by $q$. Its comparisons are natural in $y$, in weak equivalences of $x$, and in their compositions and higher homotopies; they identify the morphisms between the localized representables with the maps induced by $q$. No enrichment, properness or combinatoriality of $\mathcal M$ is assumed.

source.place: Appendix A, paragraph immediately after Proposition A.0.3 and before Corollary A.0.4, printed p. 208 (PDF p. 215), using the local model for a representable from HAG I Lemma 4.2.2 Read online; not archived locally. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: Write $W$ for the weak equivalences of $\mathcal M$, and $C=w\mathcal U$. Apply [lem-coef-homotopy-fractions-square-criterion] both to $(\mathcal M,W)$ and to $(C,C)$. Here its two auxiliary subcategories are the trivial cofibrations and the trivial fibrations, restricted to the objects of $C$ in the second application. The span completion is the pushout $Y'=X'\amalg_XY$ of a trivial cofibration $X\to X'$; its map $Y\to Y'$ is a trivial cofibration by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. The dual cospan completion is the pullback of a trivial fibration; the right lifting property is preserved because a lifting square for the pullback projects to one for the original map, whose filler pairs with the given map to the base. Thus the pulled-back map is a trivial fibration. In the pushout square $gu=vf$, if $f$ is weak then so is $g$, since $u,v$ are weak; the dual argument gives the required condition in the pullback square. Factor any $w$ functorially as a cofibration followed by a trivial fibration. Two-out-of-three makes the cofibration trivial. Pushouts and pullbacks can be chosen functorially by their universal properties, and the factorization is functorial by hypothesis. In the application to $C$, the new pushout object is weakly equivalent to $Y$, the new pullback object to $X$, and the factorization object to its endpoints. Closure of $\mathcal U$ therefore keeps all new objects in $\mathcal U$, and every newly constructed arrow is weak. Consequently both pairs have the stated two-sided homotopy calculus. No pushout of an arbitrary weak equivalence is being used.

source.place: Proposition 8.2 and its model-category application in 8.3-8.4, printed pp. 29-30; verification for the weak-equivalence-only subcategory written out.

proof.text: For $y,x\in\mathcal U$, let $Z(y,x)=Z_{-+-}^{\mathcal M,W}(y,x)$ and $Z_C(y,x)=Z_{-+-}^{C,C}(y,x)$, with the diagram-category meaning of [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus]. An object of $Z(y,x)$ is $y\xleftarrow{a}u\xrightarrow{f}v\xleftarrow{b}x$, with $a,b\in W$. Here $\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal M)$ may be taken to be the homotopy category of $\mathcal M_\infty$: applying the universal localization property of [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization] to nerves of ordinary target categories gives exactly the ordinary localization universal property after taking homotopy classes. Its morphism in $\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal M)$ is $[b]^{-1}[f][a]^{-1}$. By [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] this is invertible exactly when $f\in W$. Indeed $[a]$ and $[b]$ are already invertible, so invertibility of the displayed composite is equivalent to invertibility of $[f]$. Both $u$ and $v$ belong to $\mathcal U$ by closure, whether or not $f$ is weak. Hence $Z_C(y,x)$ is exactly the full subcategory selected by $f\in W$. For any morphism of such zigzags the middle square is $d f=f' c$, with $c,d\in W$; two-out-of-three says that $f\in W$ if and only if $f'\in W$. There are therefore no arrows in either direction between the selected objects and the others. The nerve $NZ_C(y,x)$ is precisely the union of those components of $NZ(y,x)$ whose represented morphisms are invertible.

source.place: Sections 5.1, 6.2 and 6.3-6.4, printed pp. 24-26; explicit two-endpoint version of the equivalence-component argument.

proof.text:
Use [lem-coef-homotopy-fractions-hammock-comparison] for each of the two pairs from Step 1, and [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization] to identify their hammock mapping objects with their universal-localization mapping spaces. Write $j:NC\to C_\infty=C[C^{-1}]_\infty$. For the inclusion $C\to\mathcal M$ the square of reduction maps commutes: in either order it includes each row of the same three-arrow diagram and reduces the same hammock. The top reduction is thus $NZ_C(y,x)\to L^H(C,C)(y,x)$, and the bottom is $NZ(y,x)\to L^H(\mathcal M,W)(y,x)$, both weak homotopy equivalences. Step 2 selects exactly the preimage of the equivalence components under the bottom map: reduction represents $q(b)^{-1}q(f)q(a)^{-1}$, and an edge in an infinity category is an equivalence exactly when its homotopy-category class is invertible. Restricting a weak homotopy equivalence to a union of components and its inverse-image components remains a weak homotopy equivalence, since its bijection on components and all based homotopy-group isomorphisms restrict. It follows by two-out-of-three that the actual inclusion-induced map gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{C_\infty}(jy,jx)\simeq\operatorname{Map}^{\mathrm{eq}}_{\mathcal M_\infty}(qy,qx).$$
In particular this is the comparison induced by $q$, rather than an unpointed equivalence of spaces. The hammock node identifies actual arrows and gives compatibility with composition and its homotopies.

source.place: Proposition 6.2(i), Sections 3.1 and 3.4, and Corollary 6.4, printed pp. 20-21 and 26. The existing hammock-localization node supplies the coherent-localization interpretation.

proof.text:
Put $B=NC$ and choose a Kan replacement $r:B\to K$ using [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. By [lem-cbc-simplicial-groupoid-localization], $r$ is the universal homotopy coherent localization inverting every edge of $NC$. The hammock localization $j$ of Step 3 has exactly the same universal property by [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization]. To compare them, extend $r$ along $j$ and $j$ along $r$; full faithfulness of restriction in the two universal properties identifies both composites with the respective identities, with their coherent comparison transformations. Thus $K\simeq C_\infty$ under $NC$, and Step 3 becomes
$$\operatorname{Path}_{K}(ry,rx)\simeq\operatorname{Map}^{\mathrm{eq}}_{\mathcal M_\infty}(qy,qx).$$
This equivalence is induced by the extension of $q|_C$ and respects composition and all higher simplices. This does not use the node lem-coef-model-weak-equivalence-nerve, whose proof depends on the present item.

source.place: Appendix A, mapping-space comparison before Corollary A.0.4, printed p. 208; localization proof of that comparison via Steps 1-3, with Kerodon 01MY and 01MS for groupoid localization.

proof.text: Apply the adjunction $\mathcal N_C\dashv\mathcal S_C$ of [lem-coef-locally-constant-presheaf-slice]. Its formula gives $\mathcal N_C(h_x)=N(C/x)\to B$. The representable $h_x$ is projectively cofibrant: it is the codomain of the generating cofibration $h_x\times\partial\Delta^0\to h_x\times\Delta^0$ in [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. It remains cofibrant in $P_{\mathrm{lc}}(C)$, whose localization does not change cofibrations. Factor $N(C/x)\to B$ functorially in the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] as a trivial cofibration $N(C/x)\to T_x$ followed by a Kan fibration $T_x\to B$. Set $E_x=\mathcal S_C(T_x)$. The right Quillen functor makes $E_x$ fibrant. The adjoint map $h_x\to E_x$ is the derived unit of this Quillen equivalence, computed on a cofibrant source with a fibrant replacement of its left image; it is therefore a local weak equivalence. This supplies an actual map of simplicial presheaves and the required fibrant object. By the definition of the localized weak equivalences in the cited slice node, its local weak equivalence has exactly the mapping-into-local-Kan-objects meaning stated in the item.

source.place: Proposition A.0.3 and the paragraph immediately following it, printed pp. 207-208; construction of the local model via the derived unit instead of the cosimplicial-frame formula.

proof.text:
Here is the slice calculation including a model over the non-Kan base $B$. The terminal object $(x,1_x)$ contracts $N(C/x)$: on a chain, append its unique arrow to this object. This supplies the homotopy from the identity to the constant vertex, and projection to $B$ gives its specified homotopy to $x$. Thus $\{x\}\to N(C/x)$ is a weak equivalence over $B$. In the Cartesian simplicial Kan model structure supplied by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model], the slice enrichment has $n$-simplices maps $A\times\Delta^n\to T$ over $B$; its simplicial lifting axiom is inherited from simplicial sets because a lift respecting the target $T$ automatically respects its map to $B$. The simplicial model axiom applied to $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ gives the Kan fibration $K^{\Delta^1}\to K\times K$. Restrict its final endpoint to $rx$ to obtain $P_x\to K$, with initial endpoint as projection. The total space $P_x$ contracts to the constant path at $rx$: precomposition with $\max:[1]\times[1]\to[1]$ gives a homotopy from the identity path to that constant path while keeping its final endpoint fixed. Pull back along $r$ to get $\widetilde P_x=B\times_KP_x\to B$. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] the map $\widetilde P_x\to P_x$ is a weak equivalence, so $\widetilde P_x$ is contractible. The constant path at $rx$ gives a weak equivalence $\{x\}\to\widetilde P_x$ over $B$, and $\widetilde P_x\to B$ is a Kan fibration. Thus this is a fibrant replacement in the slice of the vertex $x$. Since every simplicial set is cofibrant, the derived slice mapping space from the vertex $y$ to the vertex $x$ is the strict fiber of this replacement at $y$, namely $\operatorname{Path}_K(ry,rx)$. Replacing the two vertices by the equivalent $N(C/y)$ and $N(C/x)$ gives
$$\operatorname{Map}^h_{\mathsf{sSet}/B}(N(C/y),N(C/x))\simeq\operatorname{Path}_K(ry,rx).$$

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.0.3 and the following four-term comparison, printed p. 208; terminal-object contraction and fibrant path model written out.

proof.text:
The evaluation and derived mapping-space comparison of [lem-coef-locally-constant-presheaf-slice], applied to the unit of Step 5 and then Step 6, now give
$$E_x(y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}^h_{P_{\mathrm{lc}}(C)}(h_y,E_x)\simeq\operatorname{Map}^h_{P_{\mathrm{lc}}(C)}(h_y,h_x)\simeq\operatorname{Map}^h_{\mathsf{sSet}/B}(N(C/y),N(C/x))\simeq\operatorname{Path}_K(ry,rx).$$
Compose with Step 4. This proves precisely the displayed value formula of the item. In particular, for an actual weak equivalence $f:y\to x$, its Yoneda map $h_y\to h_x$ goes under $\mathcal N_C$ to the functor $C/y\to C/x$ given by postcomposition with $f$. The terminal vertex $(y,1_y)$ goes to $(y,f)$, whose terminal arrow to $(x,1_x)$ is $f$ itself. Hence the slice path comparison carries this morphism to the edge $f$ of $NC$, and Steps 3-4 carry it to $q(f)$. This verifies the comparison on actual weak equivalences.

source.place: Paragraph immediately following Proposition A.0.3 and preceding Corollary A.0.4, printed p. 208; identify the actual-map comparison by the terminal arrows.

proof.text: The factorization in Step 5 is functorial in maps over $B$, hence $x\mapsto E_x$ and $h_x\to E_x$ are natural for all arrows of $C$. Evaluation is contravariantly natural in $y$. The slice node [lem-coef-locally-constant-presheaf-slice] states that its derived comparisons preserve representable morphisms, identities, composition and their homotopies. Steps 3-4 identify their other side using the universal localized functor of [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization] and the full functor-category universal property of [lem-cbc-simplicial-groupoid-localization]. Consequently these are equivalences between the mapping-space bifunctors on the localization of $C$: extending along that localization is fully faithful on coherent functor categories, so it retains the comparisons, their transformations and every higher simplex. The contractions in Step 6 express the vertex comparison for the same functors $C/x\to C/x'$; they specify the path comparison under $NC$, not a separately chosen equivalence at each pair of endpoints. Composition of the morphisms between localized representables is therefore carried to composition under the extension of $q|_C$, and Step 7 identifies its actual-arrow restriction with $q$. This proves all the stated naturality and higher-compatibility clauses. All model hypotheses on $\mathcal M$ used in Steps 1-3 were its functorial factorizations, lifting axioms and two-out-of-three; no enrichment, properness or combinatoriality was added.
